system.name: Harmonic
system.one_liner: a hardware-assisted system that enforces per-tenant RDMA performance isolation in public clouds using an FPGA-based PCIe switch

summary: This figure shows the internal architecture of the Programmable Intelligent PCIe Switch (PIPS), the FPGA-based hardware component that lets Harmonic monitor tenant RDMA behavior through PCIe. PIPS comprises five modules housed in a dashed FPGA boundary: a PCIe Switch (M2) that forwards TLPs at line rate between an upstream port to the Host and a downstream port to the RNIC; a TLP Analyzer (M5) that inspects RNIC-issued DMA read/write TLP headers; a Mapping Manager (M4) and Host-PIPS Comm. Interface (M3) that synchronize address-to-object/tenant mappings with the Host's Kernel Driver (M1); and a Statistics block collecting traffic counts. Orange dashed arrows trace the asynchronous TLP-analysis path, explicitly decoupled per the caption from the switch's solid forwarding path, while solid black double arrows show Host-PIPS synchronization.
summary_zh: 该图展示了 Harmonic 中可编程智能 PCIe 交换机（PIPS）的内部架构：PCIe 交换机负责转发 TLP，TLP 分析器异步检测并匹配租户映射，映射管理器与主机内核驱动同步，虚线表示与转发路径解耦的异步分析路径。
notes: The exact endpoints of the plain-digit step labels (1/2/3) along the dashed path are inferred from the caption and module roles rather than spelled out step-by-step in the text.
